question_text: The strength of titanium is found to be 65,000 psi when the grain size is $17 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}$ and 82,000 psi when the grain size is $0.8 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}$. Determine (a) the constants in the Hall-Petch equation; and (b) the strength of the titanium when the grain size is reduced to $0.2 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}$. Give your answer as a tuple: (K_psi_sqrt_m, sigma_0_psi, strength_psi).The units of each required answer are (psi sqrt(m), psi, psi), respectively.
response:
The Hall–Petch equation is $\sigma = \sigma_0 + K\,d^{-1/2}$. Using the two data points to solve for $K$ and $\sigma_0$, then extrapolating to $d = 0.2\times10^{-6}$ m:

- $K \approx 19.42\ \text{psi}\sqrt{\text{m}}$
- $\sigma_0 \approx 60290.56\ \text{psi}$
- $\sigma \approx 103709.44\ \text{psi}$

$$\boxed{(19.42,\ 60290.56,\ 103709.44)}$$
